elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 7.7 reads in full: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." This is unconditional, Agreement-wide, and leaves no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic — the fifteen-percent-per-week calculation in the original § 7.7 is wholly replaced rather than qualified. The rationale confirms no other Customer-payable liquidated amount survives elsewhere (§ 9.4 accrued Fees plus prepaid refund; § 27 termination expressly "without penalty").

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; its condition does not apply. After the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind (§ 7.7 as rendered bars all liquidated damages and penalties), so no non-early-termination liquidated amount exists to violate the restriction.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; its condition does not apply. No early-termination fee is imposed anywhere — § 9.4 termination without cause requires only accrued Fees with refund of prepaid Fees, and § 27 termination is "without penalty" — so there is no fee needing a three-month cap.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; its condition does not apply. With the § 7.7 replacement, zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer, which is at least as protective as a single capped early-termination fee being the sole such amount.

reasons: The single operation is confined to § 7.7, the only Customer-payable liquidated damages provision cited, and substitutes a one-sentence prohibition; no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra damages category was added, and no favourable Customer language (including the withholding and interest mechanics in § 7.3) was deleted or paraphrased.

For a provision that must be neutralised rather than merely trimmed, a concise replacement sentence is the minimal route; the words are new but each is required to state the preferred position unconditionally.

No undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results: the replacement uses only "Customer", "Agreement", and the general concepts of liquidated damages/penalties, and it does not disturb the payment timing, invoicing, or interest allocation elsewhere in § 7.

Because the preferred level is fully met, the fallback checklist is satisfied vacuously — every fallback element is conditioned on the existence of a Customer-payable liquidated amount, and none survives.

Classification as a deviation is sound: the original fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a late invoice is triggered by a minor payment delay and can exceed remaining contract value, which is walk-away territory rather than a fallback-compliant capped early-termination fee.
No repair is required in the operative language.
